original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: Formal F2[GL2(F2)] rank-one-idempotent register model with free scalar GL_r(F2) mixing, but with the even order-3 target class: T_t = diag([c],...,[c]), c = ab = (ba)^2, at exactly r = t registers (t = 1, 2, 3, 4), all registers arbitrary dirty inputs restored exactly. Exact paid-call minimum; complete exclusion of every shorter even length; written sign-quotient invariants plus a free-layer screening system that is necessary only for words of length at most 3 (see README section 3); two engines (natural image and formal coefficients).
scope_change_reason: Refinement inside the card's allowed variation (fixed larger register count, specified nonabelian family F2[GL2(F2)]). The target element class is changed from the predecessor line's transposition (SWAP) targets to even order-3 targets: the sign quotient maps [c] to 1, so the inherited invariant flips from sum_i N_i = D_t to sum_i N_i = 0 and no predecessor conclusion transfers. This is not the excluded three-register abelian model.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the nonbinding bit side: no paid profile, supplier or moment changes. It prices the even-target tariff of an explicit nonabelian register alphabet, one input to whether any small-width completed saving could change the bit primitive; a q < 2t word would have been such a mechanism, and its absence through t = 4 narrows where one could live.
stop_rule: Stop after the complete t = 4 decision (all shorter even lengths excluded or a formal witness found), one calibration against the predecessor's recorded ball counts, and the written-invariant checks; do not extend to t = 5 in this session.
evidence: RECEIPT.json: minima q*(t) = 2t for t = 1, 2, 3, 4 (2, 4, 6, 8); all meets nat_hits = 0 for every shorter even length; t = r = 4 exact-depth ball-value counts 240 / 32,651 / 3,639,920 match PR1705's recorded calibration; engine B agrees with engine A on every small meet; attaining words verified exactly in M_r(F2[G]) with drop-one-call mutations failing; free-layer screening system holds on the checked attaining words and is rejected on a wrong-target control, but is not necessary for hitting words (r = 1 b a b a counterexample; README section 3). Final line: PASS_EVEN_TARGET_CNOT_CENSUS t1r1_min=2 t2r2_min=4 t3r3_min=6 t4r4_upper=8 t4r4_excluded={2: 0, 4: 0, 6: 0} balls4=240,32651,3639920 pr1705_ball_match=True no_new_kappa.
author: Aaron Wang

open_questions.question: Does the 2-calls-per-target tariff stay exact for even order-3 targets at t = r = 5 and beyond, or does cross-register sharing first pay there?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether the tariff pattern q* = 2t is a general law of the even-target line, as 3t is for SWAP targets through t = 3.
open_questions.first_step: Run the same engine at t = r = 5 (480 generators; measure the depth-3 ball first) and exclude q = 8 and q = 10 by 4+4 and 5+5 meets or a written argument.
open_questions.blocked_by: Ball growth: the r = 5 depth-3 ball is expected to exceed the r = 4 depth-3 count of 3.6e6 states by at least an order of magnitude.

open_questions.question: Can a written degree-complete kernel analysis exclude q < 2t at general t = r, without a meet? (The degree 1-3 free-layer system cannot: it is necessary only for words of length at most 3.)
open_questions.why_it_matters: A written exclusion would remove the exponential meet from the even-target line entirely.
open_questions.first_step: Compute the kernel of F -> F2[G] in degree 4 (the smallest case where the low-degree matching breaks) and re-derive conditions on the degree 1-4 layer sums there.
open_questions.blocked_by: From q = 4 on, kernel elements of degree 4 and higher absorb the low-degree mismatch (the r = 1 b a b a counterexample is the smallest instance); controlling those higher-degree kernel terms is the missing step.
